title: Dravid and Sehwag's Sons Named in India U-19 Squad for Australia Series
excerpt: Anvay Dravid and Aaryavir Sehwag will share the dressing room when India host Australia U-19 in a five-match series starting September 18 in Rajkot
body:
• The BCCI named Anvay Dravid, son of Rahul Dravid, and Aaryavir Sehwag, son of Virender Sehwag, in India's U-19 squad for a home series against Australia starting September 18
  • Anvay, a 17-year-old wicketkeeper-batter, scored 101 runs including a 67-ball 87 in two Youth ODIs against Sri Lanka earlier this year
  • Aaryavir, who hit 297 off 309 balls in the 2024 Cooch Behar Trophy, receives his first India U-19 call-up after impressing in the Delhi Premier League
  • The series comprises three Youth ODIs in Rajkot and two Youth Tests in Rajkot and Ahmedabad, running from September 18 to October 8
  • Lakshya Raichandani will captain the ODI squad, while Yashbardhan Chauhan leads the multi-day side, with the two swapping vice-captaincy roles across formats

Two of the most storied surnames in Indian cricket will share a dressing room at the junior level. The BCCI on August 27 named Anvay Dravid and Aaryavir Sehwag — sons of batting legends Rahul Dravid and Virender Sehwag — in the India U-19 squad for the upcoming home series against Australia U-19.

The five-match tour, comprising three Youth ODIs and two Youth Tests, will run from September 18 to October 8 across venues in Rajkot and Ahmedabad.

Anvay Dravid: The Quiet Accumulator

Anvay, 17, is the younger son of Rahul Dravid, widely regarded as one of India's greatest Test batters and the head coach who guided the senior team to the 2024 T20 World Cup title. A right-handed wicketkeeper-batter, Anvay has already represented India U-19, playing two Youth ODIs during a tour of Sri Lanka in July this year.

His numbers were promising: 101 runs across two innings, headlined by a composed 87 off 67 balls in Hambantota. His older brother, Samit Dravid, is an all-rounder who made his debut in the KSCA Maharaja Trophy with Mysuru Warriors in 2024, and has represented Karnataka in domestic cricket.

Anvay's selection as the second wicketkeeper in the ODI squad — alongside Rajat Baghel — suggests the selectors see him as more than a namesake. His performance against Sri Lanka on unfamiliar pitches in Hambantota earned him a spot on pure merit.

Aaryavir Sehwag: The Big Hitter Arrives

If Anvay carries echoes of his father's patience, Aaryavir Sehwag channels the elder Sehwag's aggression. This is his first India U-19 call-up, and it comes on the back of a domestic track record that already has people paying attention.

During the 2024 Cooch Behar Trophy — India's premier under-19 multi-day competition — Aaryavir hammered 297 off 309 balls against Meghalaya, an innings that included 51 fours and three sixes. The knock drew inevitable comparisons to his father, who scored a triple century against Pakistan in a 2004 Test in Multan.

"Aaryavir Sehwag has never played for India U-19. His inclusion in the squad is a maiden call-up."

— Wisden

Aaryavir has been part of the West Delhi Lions franchise in the ongoing Delhi Premier League 2026, where he has had limited opportunities so far with scores of 22 and 2. But his selection for the Australia series marks a step up, placing him in a squad preparing for five-match bilateral competition.

The Squad and Schedule

Lakshya Raichandani will captain the ODI squad, with Yashbardhan Chauhan serving as vice-captain. Their roles reverse for the multi-day fixtures: Chauhan takes charge, with Raichandani as his deputy. The leadership swap across formats is a deliberate move by the BCCI Junior Cricket Committee, giving both players captaincy experience ahead of future age-group tournaments.

The Youth ODI squad reads: Lakshya Raichandani (c), Yashbardhan Chauhan (vc), Rajat Baghel (wk), Anvay Dravid (wk), Aaryavir Sehwag, VK Vineet, Kushagra Ojha, Arjun Rajput, Manal Chauhan, V Yashveer, Rohit Yadav, Shavin Vinodh, Mohit Ulva, Chigurupati Venkata, and Kavya Patel.

All three ODIs will be played in Rajkot on September 18, 21 and 23. The first Youth Test follows on September 27-30 in Rajkot, with the second scheduled for October 5-8 at the Ahmedabad-B Ground.

Legacy, but on Their Own Terms

For Indian cricket fans, the Dravid and Sehwag names carry enormous weight. Rahul Dravid scored 13,288 Test runs and was nicknamed "The Wall" for his defensive technique. Virender Sehwag, his opening partner through India's golden Test era, took apart bowling attacks with a brand of fearless hitting rarely seen before him.

Their sons now have a chance to begin writing their own chapters. Neither has asked to carry the burden of comparison — but in Indian cricket, famous surnames are both a launchpad and a spotlight. The September series against Australia will be the first real test of whether Anvay's composure and Aaryavir's power can translate at the international junior level.

"Anvay Dravid played two Youth ODIs in Sri Lanka in July 2026, scoring 14 and a 67-ball 87 in his two games."

— Wisden
